pdvar Algebra

Documents/pdvar/matrix operations/algebra

pdvar stores affine YALMIP expressions at cell-local Bernstein labels. The examples use deterministic metadata rather than unstable YALMIP variable names.

Build affine sums and differences

Section titled “Build affine sums and differences”

Compatible grids and degrees are aligned before coefficient rows are combined. Numeric constants, affine sdpvar, and coefficient-backed pdmat operands are promoted. uplus preserves the expression; uminus negates every symbolic coefficient.

Multiply by known data

Section titled “Multiply by known data”

mtimes is allowed when decision dependence occurs on at most one converted operand. Numeric and coefficient-backed pdmat data may multiply a decision-bearing pdvar on a dimensionally valid side. An affine sdpvar also carries decision dependence after conversion.

For a quadratic decision and affine known factor on one cell,

(PA)[k]=∑i+j=k(2i)(1j)(3k)P[i]A[j],k=0,1,2,3.(PA)[k]=\sum_{i+j=k} \frac{\binom2i\binom1j}{\binom3k}P[i]A[j], \qquad k=0,1,2,3.(PA)[k]=i+j=k∑​(k3​)(i2​)(j1​)​P[i]A[j],k=0,1,2,3.

Written matrix order is preserved; P[i]A[j]P[i]A[j]P[i]A[j] is not exchanged with A[j]P[i]A[j]P[i]A[j]P[i].

L = A * P;
R = P * A;
Show the complete runnable affine-decision example
yalmip('clear')
A = pdmat({[0 1]}, {2, 3}, Degree=1);
P = pdvar(1, {[0 1]}, Degree=2);
L = A * P;
R = P * A;
fprintf('left=%d-by-%d degree=%d\n', size(L,1),size(L,2),L.Degree);
fprintf('right=%d-by-%d degree=%d\n', size(R,1),size(R,2),R.Degree);
% left=1-by-1 degree=3
% right=1-by-1 degree=3

Validation and operation boundaries

Section titled “Validation and operation boundaries”
  • Products with decision dependence on both sides are rejected as nonlinear.
  • Products with rate dependence on both sides are rejected.
  • Affine sdpvar multiplication requires the pdvar side to contain no decision dependence.
  • Numeric and pdmat promotion still requires compatible physical bounds and matrix dimensions.
  • Numeric or known data may multiply a derivative object while preserving its rate rows.
